title: Chocolate Sprinkle Brigadeiros
summary: Soft, fudgy Brazilian chocolate truffles made from condensed milk, cocoa and butter, rolled in chocolate sprinkles and served in paper cases.

ingredients.item: unsalted butter, plus a little for the plate and your hands
fine sea salt or table salt

ingredients.note: check the label; many contain soya lecithin or traces of milk

steps.title: Cook slowly
steps.text: Put the condensed milk, cocoa, butter and salt in the saucepan over low heat. Stir constantly for 15-20 min, scraping the base and corners so nothing catches.

steps.title: Check it is thick enough
steps.text: It is ready when it is very thick and glossy and slides away from the base in one mass when you tilt the pan. A line drawn through it with the spatula should stay open for 2-3 seconds.

steps.title: Cool and chill
steps.text: Scrape it onto the buttered plate, leave for 20 min, then refrigerate for about 1 h, until firm enough to roll.

steps.title: Roll the balls
steps.text: Rub a little butter on your hands and roll level tablespoons, about 18 g each, into 24 smooth balls.

steps.title: Coat in sprinkles
steps.text: Roll each ball in the bowl of sprinkles, pressing gently so they cling all over, and set them in the paper cases.

tips: The most common mistake is stopping too early; undercooked mixture stays too soft to roll and slumps in the cases, so wait for the trail test.
Keep the heat low and never stop stirring, or the condensed milk catches and tastes burnt.
Use true chocolate vermicelli rather than waxy coloured sprinkles for the classic taste.
If the mixture sticks to your hands, chill it for another 20 min.
storage: Best on the day they are made. Keep in an airtight box in the fridge for up to 5 days and bring to room temperature for 20 min before serving.
